subject: general
question: Who became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, which is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces in Nov 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Col Sunita BS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Col Sunita BS** became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC) in Delhi Cantt in **November 2023**.
 
• The **Armed Forces Transfusion Centre** is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Indian Armed Forces, playing a crucial role in providing blood and its components for military personnel.
 
• Col Sunita BS has a distinguished career in **transfusion medicine** and has contributed significantly to improving blood collection and storage processes in the Armed Forces.
 
• This landmark achievement aligns with the Armed Forces' efforts to promote **gender equality** and increase women's representation in leadership roles.
 
• The appointment highlights the growing recognition of women's capabilities in commanding critical operational roles in the military.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC):**

 
 
• The AFTC is responsible for the collection, testing, storage, and distribution of blood and blood products for the Armed Forces.
 
• It operates under strict quality standards to ensure safe and efficient blood transfusion services.
 
• The centre supports military hospitals and field units during peacetime and wartime operations.
 
 
 
• **Transfusion Medicine:**
 
 
• It is a specialized branch of medicine focused on the transfusion of blood and its components.
 
• Key areas include blood donation, compatibility testing, and the management of blood storage and supply.
 
• Advancements in transfusion medicine have significantly reduced the risks of transfusion-transmitted infections.
 
 
 
• **Women in the Armed Forces:**
 
 
• Women were first inducted into the Indian Armed Forces in **1992** in non-combat roles.
 
• Over the years, their participation has expanded to include combat support and operational roles.
 
• Recent policy changes have allowed women to take on leadership positions, such as commanding units and serving in combat roles.
 
 
 
• **Gender Equality in the Military:**
 
 
• The Indian government and Armed Forces have taken steps to increase women's representation, including granting them permanent commissions in various branches.
 
• These initiatives aim to break gender stereotypes and promote equality within the ranks.
